A.B.S. (North American Indians)
English, A.B.S., 2289-1560
The A.B.S. were a tribe of the Algonquian people who inhabited southern New York and northern Pennsylvania during the late Middle Ages. Their territory stretched from Cape Cod to the Delaware River in present day Maryland and southeastern Virginia. Their name is derived from the Algonquian word "munjag," meaning "horse" or "cow." The English language has borrowed many elements from French, which was also adopted by the Iroquois. They migrated westward into present-day Ohio and Tennessee and eventually settled on large portions of the area around Lake Erie.
Their name means "crossed," and refers to a group of people who lived in one section of Lake Erie and later along the coast. They are called the A.B.S. or the "B.D.'s," because they were noted for their ability to travel through water without fear of being caught up in boats or even killed. They are known as the D'S.

The Moon and the Sun
A story about a son of a farmer who grew wheat in his field. He was particularly interested in learning more about the role that ancient civilizations played in the development of our planet. His first book, The Life of St. John the Baptist (1694), was the most influential book on earth history and religion.
In it he wrote:
“I saw the moon and the sun… I felt it and made my very own paper. My father told me that there was one for each of us. I thought this would be good advice, but then he noticed something had gone wrong and said ‘Let’s do some research.’”
He further added: “I never did anything else except to help him look at the moon and see if it was an object of worship or not. I had a friend tell me that it was a rock and it looked like the moon. But I thought it was a stone and just went off and peered through the hole.”
And he returned: “It is true that the earth has always been round in its interior. As we have seen, it is always round as well.”

“An Old Woman’s Journey to New York” by Alice Lewis and Frances Yates
Is it a true story?
It seems that it is.
In 1920, Alice Lewis went to Harlem in search of her beloved “The World Book,” and met her mother who was born there.
Lewis had a passion for history, and through her mother she became an art teacher and an illustrator. She soon developed a love for literature and started writing stories about it. Her inspiration came from Alice.
Lewis published many books on the subject, including “Alice in Wonderland” (1924), which tells the story of her childhood journey to New York City with her mother. She also wrote about it in her book The Art of the Month: A Memoir.
In 1927, Lewis moved into her new home in Harlem, where she continued to work as a freelance artist until she was hired by the publisher Harper & Brothers. In 1936 she founded the first art museum in New York City called the Museum of American Art. It is now known as the Art Institute of Chicago.

From increased dependence on fossil fuels to increasing population pressures, the effects of climate change are a key factor in how people react to extreme weather events such as floods, droughts, wildfires, or heat waves. These changes are made possible through greenhouse gases emitted during the burning of fossil fuels, and may even contribute to global warming.

The Great Ice Age is the most comprehensive and detailed study of ice ages to date, which reveals how glaciers developed over vast areas.
"I have always been fascinated by ice age studies," said Darren Scott, a glaciologist at the University of Calgary in Canada. "You can't just go out there and look at the ice for a moment, but you can see what happened over thousands of years."
Scott's research includes both mapping glacial deposits and ground-level measurements of sediment flows and bedrock samples that are deposited on land. He compared these data with current findings of previous research about Greenland and Antarctica and found that the ice sheets formed from around 350 million years ago and that they were predominantly composed of continental material (geologically younger than today).
"This study is a strong demonstration that glaciers are active during periods of high precipitation," he said. "We have mapped the precise locations of Greenland and Antarctica using modern methods. We've also used a new technique called radiocarbon dating to determine the exact timing of glacier retreats and the direction of ice flow. This shows us that glaciers grew in this way."

When the World War II Tigers were a fighting force, they weren't part of the traditional forces but were part of the National Guard.
The story is that the men from the National Guard moved into the country to join in their war effort. The National Guard was an organization formed by soldiers who were trained in the United States Army Corps of Engineers and served under the leadership of General Winfield Scott and his staff during World War I.
In 1920, after receiving their first order, the U.S. Navy decided to open an infantry battalion for service overseas, giving them support with weapons and equipment. It was this group that eventually became the National Guard.
While there are no official records on how the National Guard got its name, it does appear to have been derived from the French word "tiger" which means "a mule".
During the Spanish Civil War, most of the National Guard's manpower came from Spain. After the Spanish Civil War, the Spanish government decided to divide the military between the United States and the United Kingdom.

The sun reflects blue light into space. It’s only possible to see it from Earth, but it takes a huge amount of energy to shine the light back on us. Fortunately, most of this energy is used to create the hydrogen gas in stars and galaxies – the stuff that helps drive our Universe. In fact, stars are so efficient at producing hydrogen from hydrogen atoms that they can produce visible light when there’s a massive star nearby. The hydrogen glow is one of the best-known examples of how the human eye works because it has been studied by astronomers for years.
This is where the science comes in. Astronomers know that the stars have hydrogen in their cores, which absorbs ultraviolet radiation and causes them to glow green. As this happens, a small amount of hydrogen emits infrared light, creating a powerful spectrum of colors in the spectrum of the Sun.
When we look up close, our eyes get a good view of the sky. They also know that the stars are glowing red, giving us a clear picture of what lies beyond. When we look up, we’ll notice how much of the starlight hits our eyes: 103 million times more than that is reflected back in the infrared light.

“I want to explore if we can predict future coral reef conditions,” she said. “We’re interested in whether coral reefs are more resilient or less vulnerable than our current models suggest.”
The research team also wants to see if coral reefs form in the same way as ecosystems do. In addition, they want to understand how different factors affect the growth and health of coral reefs.
